entities.name: PMID:27507659
observations: Swedish register-based sibling study of birth cohorts 1987–1994 examined later birth order versus first-born siblings and alcohol- or narcotics-related hospitalization using Cox models with sibling fixed effects.

Before age 20, alcohol-related hospitalization was approximately 47% higher for second-borns (HR 1.47) and 65% higher for third-borns (HR 1.65) versus first-borns; narcotics hospitalization showed a similar monotonic pattern, without reported narcotics-specific estimates in the available abstract.
Associations after age 20 were directionally similar but weaker.

entities.name: PMID:36091296
observations: Swedish national 1953 birth cohort and sibling study followed ages 30–55 for alcohol- or narcotics-attributable hospitalization or death using patient and cause-of-death registers.

Bivariate hazards increased with higher birth order for both outcomes, but associations disappeared after adjustment for familial-background characteristics in between-family and within-family fixed-effects models.

entities.name: Early birth-order risk
observations: In Swedish birth cohorts 1987–1994, later-born siblings had higher alcohol-related hospitalization hazards before age 20 than first-born siblings; approximately HR 1.47 for second-born and HR 1.65 for third-born.
The same study reported a similar increasing pattern for narcotics-related hospitalization, but exact narcotics-specific estimates were unavailable in the retrieved abstract.

entities.name: Midlife null after adjustment
observations: In Swedish adults followed from ages 30–55, higher birth order was not independently associated with alcohol- or narcotics-attributable hospitalization or death after adjustment for familial-background characteristics.
